item.description:
You've never played UNO like this before! Now with a Jurassic World theme, the rules are similar to those of regular UNO Attack, but this game features the "Attack! Attack!" command card that offers an exciting and unpredictable way to play UNO. If you draw that card you’ll have to push the button on the Dilophosaurus shooter, and you’ll either be the target of a stream of UNO Attack Jurassic World cards, or you will get lucky and nothing will happen! But if you’re not so lucky, the shooter will fire a stream of cards that you have to add to your hand! And when the shooter is launching cards, it makes a variety of funny sounds that add energy and silliness to the game. UNO Attack Jurassic World adds speed and surprise to the game because you never know when an attack is coming! The goal is still to get rid of all the cards in your hand, and when you’re down to one card, don’t forget to yell, “UNO!” Contains 112 cards, Dilophosaurus shooter, and instructions. The unit is both portable and designed to help with storage—you can keep the cards right inside the shooter!
Now Jurassic World fans can play a special version of UNO Attack!: The "Attack! Attack!" card - When this card is played, whoever played it gets to call any color and then choose ANY OTHER PLAYER in the game to “Attack.” The Dilophosaurus Card Launcher is rotated to face the chosen player, and then “attacking” player gets to press down on the Dilophosaur’s nose twice. The player being “attacked” must keep all the cards that come out of the launcher. The game then continues with the next player in regular rotation (the second player to the left – or right in Reverse rotation - of the player who played the Wild Attack-Attack card).
The goal is to get rid of all the cards in your hand, and the first player or team to 500 wins. When you’re down to one card, don’t forget to yell “UNO”!
—description from the publisher

item.description:
Witches Dominion: Arena Edition is an intense, self-contained tactical magic duelling game that strips the systems of the Witches Dominion full universe down to its purest mechanical bones.
Set in a dark fantasy crucible overseen by Archaia the Enchanted Witch, the game features an immersive atmosphere where 4 legendary witches are tested in pure, brutal combat.
Players can choose from the four legendary characters (Celestia, Seraphina, Lilith, or Nyx) each representing a completely distinct elemental philosophy and a unique, innate magical resilience formula. Gameplay is fast, direct, and completely eliminates complex board setups or territorial management in favour of focused, tactical card play.
The game operates on a high-stakes HP/MP Economy, where witches spend to activate personal character abilities, cast devastating deck spells, or consume alchemical potions.
Spellcasting requires a 12 sided die (d12) to clear a specific success threshold. While successful spells trigger the defender's innate passive resilience to automatically reduce incoming magical damage, raw physical combat entirely bypasses these barriers. Repelling a direct physical hit allows the defender to execute a punishing, immediate counterattack, creating an endless, reactive tug of war for momentum.
The game includes a dedicated Signature Roll Rule tied to each witch's most powerful starred ability. Activating a Signature allows the player to roll the d12 twice and take the higher result, heavily shifting the mathematical probability of success into the caster's favour and rewarding decisive execution.
Strategic depth is found in balancing these high impact character abilities with the fluctuating contents of the shared 77-card Battle Deck, which features a volatile mix of universal and alignment restricted elemental spells, potions, and one-time creature summons. Victory is claimed through one of two distinct, chosen game modes. In Elimination Mode, players engage in a fast, decisive race to reduce all opposing health pools to zero with no respawning permitted. For a deeper tactical experience, Influence Mode shifts the win condition to a race to 20 Influence Points. In this mode, players accumulate permanent points by successfully executing counterattacks, playing rare gem cards, and landing massive damage strikes, while eliminated witches continuously respawn to keep the battlefield in a constant state of fluid warfare.
—description from the designer

In Agricola, you're a farmer in a wooden shack with your spouse and little else. At first, on a turn, your family gets to take only two actions, one for you and one for your spouse, as might be found among all the possibilities on a farm: plowing fields; collecting materials; building fences, and so on. There are numerous choices available, and while the game progresses you'll have more and more, as each round a new action card is flipped over, offering one more possible action. You might think about having kids in order to get more work accomplished but first you'll need to expand your house to make room - and what are you going to feed all the little rug rats?
The game supports many levels of complexity, mainly through the distribution of cards which represent Minor Improvements and Occupations. In the beginner's version (called the Family Variant in the U.S. release) these cards are not used at all. For advanced play, the U.S. release includes three levels of both types of cards; Basic (E-deck), Interactive (I-deck), and Complex (K-deck), and the rulebook encourages players to experiment with the various decks and mixtures thereof. Aftermarket decks such as the Z-Deck and the L-Deck also exist. Each player starts with a hand of 7 Occupation cards (of more than 160 total) and 7 Minor Improvement cards (of more than 140 total) that he/she may use during the game if they fit into his/her strategy.
Agricola is a turn-based game, and the problem to be overcome is that each available action can be taken by only one player each round so it's important to be careful about your choices. There are countless strategies, some of which depend on your hand of cards.
The winner is the player with the most Victory Points from the Improvements made on his farm.
-description originally from BoardgameNews
